correctness.rationale: For the explicitly defined, occupied-center iid-neighbor dynamics the symmetric point is fixed, and the orientation-permutation-equivariant derivative is scalar on the two-dimensional tangent space. Conditional on m occupied sites I re-enumerated the derivatives without multinomial weights: fix one position first to heading 1 and then to heading 2, average the difference of each event indicator over the 3^(m−1) other words, and sum over the differentiated positions. For the tied-and-central-1 event the center derivative and each neighbor derivative are treated separately. This gave unique-plurality numerators (1,2,12,36,120,420,1330) and tied-and-central-1 numerators (0,1,0,6,6,30,80), with denominators 3^(m−1). Binomial mixing gives P,T. The scalar derivative of the total tied-event probability is zero by exchange symmetry, so the reorientation derivatives are (1−3η/2)P and (1−3η/2)P+(1−η)T. The flow subtracts 1 from each rate. In the representation s=ρ/(1−ρ), the polynomial (1+s)^6(P−1)/s has a negative constant and strictly positive higher coefficients, so there is exactly one positive root; bisection gives ρ*=0.212447606903894 to the displayed precision. For I, the first two binomial-mixture entries of a_m+b_m are 1 and every subsequent entry exceeds 1. Thus P+T−1>0 at all 0<ρ≤1 and its leading term comes from two occupied neighbors, 15ρ²·(1/3)=5ρ². The strictly positive slope magnitude 3P/2+T gives a unique threshold in (0,1), asymptotic to (10/3)ρ². At ρ=1, P=1330/729 and T=80/729 give 601/1995 and 681/2075; at ρ=ρ*,η=0 the random-tie rate is exactly zero, not strictly stable. These checks establish the intrinsic closures defined in the frozen record, independently of the spatial paper's notation or dynamics.
